listening.title: Finding your seat at the theatre
listening.part: Part 2 · Listening to a Daily Life Conversation
listening.setting: A theatre usher helps a patron find their seat before a show
listening.speaker: Patron ↔ Usher
listening.transcript:
USHER: Good evening! Let me check your ticket... You're in Section D, Row K, Seat 14.
PATRON: Great, how do I get there from the lobby?
USHER: Walk straight through the double doors, then continue through the cross aisle at the back of the orchestra level.
PATRON: Is that the row right behind the front section, Section A?
USHER: Not quite. Section D is the center rear block, positioned behind Section A, between the left and right side sections — Section B is on the left, and Section C is on the right.
PATRON: My seat is number 14 — is that near the aisle or closer to the middle of the row?
USHER: Row K has twenty seats numbered left to right, so seat 14 is on the far side, nearer the aisle that borders Section C, not the aisle near Section B.
PATRON: Are there any emergency exits close to Section D?
USHER: Yes — the nearest exits for Section D are the two at the far corners near the cross aisle, not the ones up near the stage, which are really only convenient for Section A.
PATRON: And if I need the restroom at intermission?
USHER: The restrooms are just past the lobby doors where you came in, so from Section D you'd head back the way you entered, through the cross aisle.
PATRON: One more thing — is the balcony a good option if I come back another time?
USHER: The balcony is actually the section closest to the lobby, right behind the cross aisle, so it's the quickest to reach, but it's also the farthest section from the stage.
PATRON: Thanks so much for your help!
USHER: Enjoy the show!
listening.imageAlt: Theatre seating chart showing the stage, Sections A, B, C, and D, the balcony, cross aisle, exits, and the lobby entrance
